readings.summary: Implement the core formatter-generation feature only: a parameterless GeneratedMessagePackFormatter attribute enables generation into a body-less partial formatter class, using contractless public-member serialization unless T's existing attributes specify otherwise.
readings.code_difference: Add the attribute and generator support for cross-assembly T and semicolon-only partial classes, but do not add SurrogateType, a key-mapping surface, or generate/copy MessagePack attributes into Project A.

readings.summary: Implement the core feature together with the discussed surrogate-type mechanism so callers can specify keys and settings through a Project B surrogate when Project A cannot reference MessagePack.
readings.code_difference: In addition to the core generation support, expose a settable SurrogateType property on GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute and make the generator read the surrogate's members and attributes, mapping them to T's properties by name.

output.quote: AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

readers.framing: the person who filed this issue, later checking whether what shipped is what they asked for

readings.summary: Add the attributed partial-class formatter generation with contractless fallback and support for MessagePack attributes already present on T, without adding a new way to specify keys or Union settings for an attribute-free external type.
readings.code_difference: The new attribute only marks the formatter class, and the generator inspects T directly; it has no SurrogateType property or other attribute-customization mechanism beyond the existing behavior.

readings.summary: Provide the same formatter generation and also support the proposed surrogate-type mechanism so callers in Project B can configure property keys and other settings for T without modifying Project A.
readings.code_difference: The attribute exposes a SurrogateType option, and the generator and relevant analyzers read member settings from that surrogate and map them to T by property name when generating the formatter.

output.quote: For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

readers.framing: a QA engineer who has to write acceptance tests for this requirement before any code exists

readings.summary: Add the basic formatter-generation feature: the attribute and generator support body-less partial formatter classes for referenced types, using public contractless members by default and honoring any existing MessagePack attributes, without adding a surrogate-based configuration API.
readings.code_difference: The generator emits Serialize/Deserialize implementations into the annotated class and derives keys solely from T and its existing attributes; GeneratedMessagePackFormatter has no SurrogateType property or surrogate-member mapping logic.

readings.summary: Provide the same formatter generation plus the suggested SurrogateType option so callers can supply keys and other MessagePack settings through a surrogate type, with members matched to T by property name.
readings.code_difference: In addition to basic generation, the attribute exposes a SurrogateType property and the generator reads the surrogate's members and attributes, maps them to T by property name, and uses those settings when emitting the formatter.

output.quote: AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.
